newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 to $15 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 to $15 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 to $15 per tonne higher on Friday, on the heels of a strong performance in London overnight, traders said.

London cocoa futures were higher early Friday, underpinned by weak sterling. At the midday break, LIFFE September was up 15 stg, to the high of 1,026 stg, after ranging from 1,029 to 1,011 stg. December also rose 15 stg, to 1,056 stg.

Sterling slipped to a 10-month low against the U.S. dollar and shed more than five pfennigs against the German mark overnight, jolted by indications from the Bank of England that further interest rate rises were unlikely.
On Thursday, New York cocoa futures ended unchanged to firmer, consolidating recent sharp losses. Traders said the market appeared oversold and could be due for a correction.
CSCE September rose $2 per tonne, to $1,460, after ranging between $1,470 and $1,445. Second-month December closed unchanged, at $1,504, while the back months ended flat to up $2.
On the charts, traders said September faced resistance near $1,475, while Thursday's low of $1,445 provided good support.
